answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, limiting influence that cannot escape a region. A sybil set S forms a sparse external cut with low conductance φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/vol(S), since internal attestations dominate. Mixing and min-cut transitivity bounds therefore cap honest support entering S and its aggregate voting weight, even when timber-thick links surround a hollow core or grove of colluding identities.
